- Extensive yellowing/interveinal chlorosis
- Scattered dark brown/purplish-brown spots throughout
- Necrosis concentrated toward the leaf tip
- Veins appear to retain some green color

Sudden_death_syndrome shows interveinal chlorosis with necrosis — somewhat similar. Septoria_brown_spot shows yellowing with scattered dark spots — very close match. Downy_mildew doesn't match. Let me check Cercospora.

Key observations from reference images:
- **Cercospora**: Dark purple-black diffuse patches on green leaves — doesn't match well
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Discrete circular spots with gray centers on green leaves — doesn't match
- **Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus**: Yellow blotches near veins on mostly green leaves — partial match
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Yellowing leaves with scattered small dark brown/black spots — very close match
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Interveinal chlorosis with necrosis — partial match but more vein-bounded

The test image shows a fully yellowed/chlorotic leaf with scattered dark brown spots distributed across the surface, which is the hallmark presentation of **Septoria_brown_spot**. The pattern — diffuse yellowing with small dark spots scattered throughout — matches the Septoria reference (especially top-left panel) more closely than SDS (which has more pronounced interveinal pattern with green veins).
